readings.t: 어제 엄마하고 시장에 갔어요. 시장에는 사람이 많았어요. 우리는 과일하고 생선을 샀어요. 그리고 떡볶이를 먹었어요. 조금 매웠지만 정말 맛있었어요.
readings.r: Eoje eommahago sijange gasseoyo. Sijangeneun sarami manasseoyo. Urineun gwailhago saengseoneul sasseoyo. Geurigo tteokbokkireul meogeosseoyo. Jogeum maewotjiman jeongmal masisseosseoyo.

tr.fr: Hier je suis allée au marché avec ma mère. Il y avait beaucoup de monde. Nous avons acheté des fruits et du poisson. Puis nous avons mangé des tteokbokki. C'était un peu épicé mais vraiment bon.
tr.en: Yesterday I went to the market with my mum. There were lots of people. We bought fruit and fish. Then we ate tteokbokki. It was a bit spicy but really tasty.

readings.title: 한글날
readings.t: 10월 9일은 한글날이에요. 세종대왕은 백성들이 쉽게 글을 읽고 쓸 수 있도록 한글을 만들었어요. 한글은 과학적인 문자로 알려져 있어서, 외국인도 며칠 만에 읽는 법을 배울 수 있어요.
readings.r: Siwol gurireun Hangeullarieyo. Sejongdaewangeun baekseongdeuri swipge geureul ilgo sseul su itdorok Hangeureul mandeureosseoyo. Hangeureun gwahakjeogin munjaro allyeojyeo isseoseo, oegugindo myeochil mane ingneun beobeul baeul su isseoyo.

tr.fr: Le 9 octobre est le jour du Hangeul. Le roi Sejong a créé le hangeul pour que le peuple puisse lire et écrire facilement. Le hangeul est connu comme une écriture scientifique : même les étrangers peuvent apprendre à le lire en quelques jours.
tr.en: October 9th is Hangul Day. King Sejong created Hangul so that ordinary people could read and write easily. Hangul is known as a scientific script, so even foreigners can learn to read it in a few days.

body.en: Age determines politeness level. People often ask your age right away to know how to speak to you.

body.en: Wait for the eldest to start eating. Rice and soup are eaten with a spoon, side dishes (banchan) with chopsticks.
